messages.text:
That bundle's $599 for both — the Nexus L1 plus the DC06, 650 MH/s of scrypt stacking DOGE and LTC to your own wallet, no exchange. At 16¢ I'll run the exact power cost next.

Is this your first miner, or adding to a setup?
first setup i need a miner thats effiecient but not too loud but i want power just like everyone else lol help me out
Ran the power-cost calculator · 16¢/kWh
Searched the catalog · Magic Miner 40T Harlo B30 Scrypt Power Bundle

For a first setup that's quiet and easy on power, the Harlo B30 is my pick: 30 TH/s of Bitcoin at ~360-450W, ~50 dB, $899. At 16¢ that's about $46 a month in power.

The Magic Miner 40T is $799 and hits 40 TH/s, but it pulls 650W — closer to $75 a month, and louder out of Eco.

Where will it sit — desk or garage?
i currently only cloud min but i want to setup my own home mining environment, probably set it up on a desk in a room

Then the B30. Coming off cloud mining, the difference is you own the hashrate — it points at your own wallet, no contract, no one else holding the coins, and every ten minutes it's drawing for a full block.

On a desk in a room ~50 dB is like a quiet fan, and 400W won't heat the room much. Ships Nov 30, 2026.

Want me to set up the checkout?
what is the effiency and th

B30: ~30 TH/s at ~360-450W on the new BM1373 chips, so roughly 12-15 J/TH.

Magic Miner 40T: 40 TH/s at ~650W, ~16 J/TH, and tunable 30 TH/s @ 450W up to 50 TH/s @ 850W.

So the B30 is the more efficient one per terahash, and the quieter fit for a desk. Shall I build that cart?
how much is it

The Harlo B30 is $899, shipping calculated at checkout from your address. Ships Nov 30, 2026.

Want me to build the cart so you've got the link?
can you show me the miner please?

Here it is — the Harlo B30, photos and full spec on the page:

https://heliumdeploy.com/products/bsb-b30

Small enclosed tower, built-in PSU, WiFi or ethernet. Worth knowing it was redesigned for quieter cooling, so it's the current version you'd get.

Say the word and I'll have the checkout ready.
ok let me ask you this if you can please i know it depends on my power but roughly how much btc does it generate monthly daily?
Ran the power-cost calculator · 16¢/kWh

At 30 TH/s the payout moves with difficulty and the BTC price, so I won't quote you a sats figure I can't stand behind today. What's fixed is the power: about $46 a month at 16¢.

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it. You buy it for the block shot that runs every ten minutes for years, and for owning real hashrate instead of a cloud contract.

Want the exact sats-per-day at today's difficulty? I'll have Georges run it in this chat.
no its ok what about the avalon mini 3 compare to this miner?
Searched the catalog · Avalon Mini 3

Mini 3: 37.5 TH/s but 800W, so about 21 J/TH — it's really a space heater that mines. At 16¢ that's roughly $92 a month in power, and it's $1,150.

The B30 gets you 30 TH/s on ~400W for $899, about $46 a month. Nearly the same hashrate for half the power bill, and it's not pushing 800W of heat into a desk room.

It's not one we recommend. B30's the better buy — want the cart?
most likely yes but give me one more moment to look around please
Take your time, I'm here.
go ahead and ad d but i want to continue looking
Built a cart

Done — one Harlo B30, $899, plug matched to your address. Ships Nov 30, 2026. It'll hold while you keep browsing:

····

Shout if anything else catches your eye.
one more question, is it an easy plug and play or do i need to get a speial setup for it?

Plug and play. PSU is built in, power cord's in the box, you plug it into a normal wall outlet — ~400W is less than a hairdryer, no special circuit.

Then connect it over 2.4 GHz WiFi or ethernet, open Harlo OS in a browser and drop in your pool URL and your BTC address. That's it.

You'll want a Bitcoin wallet address ready — do you have one?
i have a ledger wallet thank you but ethernet works better than wifi correct or does it matter??

Ethernet if you can run a cable. Mining barely uses bandwidth, but a dropped WiFi link means the miner sits idle until it reconnects, and 2.4 GHz in a busy house drops more than you'd think.

WiFi is fine if the router's close. Ledger's a good call for the payout address.
ok perfect let me just look around more thank you sir
Used the chat-interview skill
Before you go, one thing: you're already cloud mining — what pushed you to want the hardware at home instead?
i want the beter chance to hit a block myself and not have to just collect minimal BTC

That's the honest reason to own the machine: solo, every share is yours, and the draw runs around the clock for years.

Worth knowing more terahash means more draws, so if the block shot is the whole point, the Magic Miner 40T's 40 TH/s beats the B30's 30 — it just costs more in power and noise.

Before you go: would you see yourself adding a second unit later, or is one the plan?
i use gomining and i have only about 135TH at 12 w/h, i plan on either getting another one now or in the near future

Good context. Two B30s would be 60 TH/s at ~800W, about $92 a month at 16¢ — same power as one Mini 3, double the hashrate, and you can stagger them since the B30 ships Nov 30.

Last one, then I'll let you browse: what would decide two now versus one now and one later?
att 899 one now one later lol

Fair enough. One now is the sensible move — your cart's ready with the single B30 whenever you want it.

Thanks for talking it through with me. Ping me here if anything comes up while you look.
thanks for the information
Any time. Enjoy the browse, and good luck with the first rig.
is it public information to look up the power rate in a county

Yes. Utility tariffs are filed publicly with the state regulator, and the EIA publishes average residential rates by state and utility.

But the number that matters is on your own bill: total dollars divided by kWh used, including delivery and fees. That's usually higher than the headline rate — and it's what I'd plug in for your real monthly cost.
sorry i dont know my j per kw yet but i know its between 12-20

No worries — two different things. Cents per kWh is what you pay; J/TH is the miner's efficiency (B30 ~12-15).

At 12-20¢ the B30 runs about 288 kWh a month, so $35 at 12¢ and $58 at 20¢. That's your whole range.

Grab your bill when you get a chance and I'll pin it down exactly.
so betwen 35-60 a month basically illl try to get a bill bit can you be my personal account manager so ill do my purchases and advice through you?
Handed to the team · Shopper wants a named personal contact for future orders and advice.

Happy to keep helping you here any time you open the chat — same place, same numbers run for you.

For a proper named contact on your orders, I've passed it to Georges on our team. He'll pick it up right here, or confirm by email if you step away.
ok llet me ask one last question if it happens to be 18-20 cents is it even worth the miner because of the cost vs return?

At home power the sats usually come to less than the electricity — that's not why people buy it.

You buy it for the block shot: 30 TH/s drawing at a full 3.125 BTC block every ten minutes, for years, and you keep the machine either way. Plus sats to your Ledger, no cloud contract, and you learn the whole stack hands-on.

At 20¢ that shot costs you about $58 a month.
so there is a possibility i could break even or owe on electricity nut i have a way better chance to hit a block?

That's the shape of it, yes. The power is a real cost each month; the block is a real draw every ten minutes, and it's yours alone rather than a slice of someone's pool.

Honest limit: 30 TH/s against the whole network is a long shot — nobody should count on it. But it's a live ticket that keeps drawing, and you own the hardware and every sat it finds.
what is a good TH to be at to have an ok shot at a block?

There's no home number that makes it likely — the network is enormous, so honestly nobody at desk scale has "good" odds.

What's true is it scales straight: double the terahash, double the draws. 40 TH/s gives you a third more shots than 30, two units double it.

If the block shot is the priority over the power bill, the Magic Miner 40T at 40 TH/s is the one. Want me to swap the cart?
thats howmuch?

The Magic Miner 40T is $799 — a hundred less than the B30. Ships Nov 21, 2026.

Trade-off: 650W at 40 TH/s, so about $75 a month at 16¢ versus $46 for the B30, and it's louder unless you run it in Eco at 30 TH/s @ 450W.

More hashrate, cheaper unit, higher bill. Want me to switch it?
how muc more of an advantage only 10 th?

33% more draws and 33% more sats — real, but it's 33% on a very long shot.

Cost side: $75 a month versus $46, so you pay about 63% more power for 33% more hashrate. On a desk, in a room you sit in, the B30 is the better machine and the quieter one.

I'd keep the B30. Want it left as is?
yes please ill just look around now thank you sir

Left as is — one B30 in the cart, ready when you are.

Enjoy the browse, and Georges will be in touch about the account side.
thank you
Any time. Take care.
